title: Exact transport of module-valued normalized supported Hom
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, let (C,J) and (D,J') be sites with terminal objects and restriction arrows j and j', and assume the categories of sheaves of A-modules are Grothendieck abelian. Let B, B' be supported representing sheaves, with constant restrictions rho, rho', and evaluation- and cocycle-normalized supported-Hom comparisons N,N' as in [lem-pur-supported-hom-cocycle-normalization]. Let L be an additive exact functor between these sheaf categories, d:LB ≅ B', and tau:Gamma_j → L Gamma_j'. Suppose evaluation satisfies theta'(d^-1 Lf)=tau(theta(f)) for every morphism f:B→M. For every bounded-below derived object K and every integer a, the module-valued right-derived support map b induced by tau satisfies chi'(H^a(b)(x))=single(d^-1)·(L single)^-1·DL(chi(x))·shift_L. Here b is precisely rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange with both exact identity-functor normalizations; all comparisons are the canonical single-complex and shift comparisons.

source.place: Section 9, Ext proof of Theorem 9.4 and Example 9.5; module-valued refinement of the transport step of lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback; Stacks derived.tex Tags 05TI and 070I for injective resolutions and roof formulas

proof.text: For an injective representative I of K, choose an injective resolution e:LI→R. The defining unit factorization for rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange identifies the support pullback, after the canonical derived isomorphism DL(QI)≅QR, with the cohomology of tau_I followed by Gamma_j'(e).

Represent a cohomology class by a cycle y. The normalized comparison gives its unique f:B→I^a. Naturality of evaluation and its assumed compatibility with tau identify the transported cycle with d^-1 Lf e^a. Normalize on the injective complex R. Exact termwise transport sends the single-complex cocycle of f to that of d^-1 Lf e^a, by checking its degree-zero component. Cancel the canonical derived resolution isomorphism. The Hom-map is the existing representableTransportHom construction of [lem-pur-derived-representable-transport]; its abelian-group-valued transport theorem is not applied.

Every bounded-below derived object has an injective representative. Use naturality of the two normalized identifications, of the base-change transformation, and of the exact functor shift comparison to transfer the identity to K. No preservation of injectives by L is required.

proof_origin.place: Section 9 Ext proof, with direct module-valued derived-unit and cocycle calculation by B8

theorem moduleSupportedHom_transport
    {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A]
    {C D : Type (u + 1)} [Category.{u} C] [Category.{u} D]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (J' : GrothendieckTopology D)
    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)]
    [HasSheafify J' (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u + 1} (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u + 1} (Sheaf J' (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))]
    {T W : C} (hT : IsTerminal T) (j : W ⟶ T)
    {T' W' : D} (hT' : IsTerminal T') (j' : W' ⟶ T')
    (B : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (B' : Sheaf J' (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))
    (rho : (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)).obj (ModuleCat.of A A) ⟶ B)
    (rho' : (constantSheaf J' (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)).obj (ModuleCat.of A A) ⟶ B')
    (N : SupportedHomCocycleNormalization J A hT j B rho)
    (N' : SupportedHomCocycleNormalization J' A hT' j' B' rho')
    (L : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) ⥤ Sheaf J' (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))
    [L.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits L] [PreservesFiniteColimits L]
    (d : L.obj B ≅ B')
    (tau : Sheaf.supportedSectionsFunctor J (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j ⟶
      L ⋙ Sheaf.supportedSectionsFunctor J' (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j')
    (heval : ∀ (M : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (f : B ⟶ M),
      N'.theta.hom.app (L.obj M) (d.inv ≫ L.map f) = tau.app M (N.theta.hom.app M f))
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))) (a : ℤ) :
    let S := Sheaf.supportedSectionsFunctor J (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j
    let S' := Sheaf.supportedSectionsFunctor J' (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j'
    let b : S.rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⟶ L.mapDerivedCategoryPlus ⋙ S'.rightDerivedFunctorPlus :=
      (Functor.rightUnitor _).inv ≫
        (Functor.isoWhiskerLeft _
          (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryPlusIdIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))).inv ≫
        Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlusBaseChange
          (G := S) (G' := S') (β := L) (γ := 𝟭 (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))
          ((Functor.rightUnitor _).hom ≫ tau)
    moduleSupportedHomCompatible J J' j j' B B' N.chi N'.chi L d b K a
